meta.drug: fenofibrate (160 mg/day, or 54 mg/day with reduced eGFR) added to open-label simvastatin
meta.sponsor: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI); study drugs donated by Abbott (fenofibrate/placebo) and Merck (simvastatin)
meta.mechanism: Fibrate; PPAR-alpha agonist that increases lipoprotein lipase-mediated lipolysis and lowers hepatic VLDL output, lowering triglycerides and modestly raising HDL-C with little LDL-C effect. ACCORD Lipid tested whether adding fenofibrate (to raise HDL-C and lower triglycerides) to a statin (to lower LDL-C) reduces cardiovascular events.
meta.indication: prevention of major cardiovascular events in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes (prior CVD, subclinical CVD or >=2 risk factors) already treated with simvastatin

n_randomized.quote: A total of 5518 patients were enrolled in the ACCORD Lipid study, with 2765 assigned to receive fenofibrate plus simvastatin and 2753 assigned to receive placebo plus simvastatin.
n_randomized.note: Registry S3 denominators 2765 / 2753. ACCORD overall enrolled 10,251 (2x2 factorial with the glycemia trial).

median_followup.note: Mean, not median (median NOT FOUND). Results: 'The mean duration of follow-up was 4.7 years for the primary outcome and 5.0 years for total rates of death.' Planned average follow-up ~5.6 years.

primary_endpoint.value: First occurrence of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary outcome was the first occurrence of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.
primary_endpoint.note: Same primary outcome in all three ACCORD trials (registry S3).

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Type 2 diabetes with HbA1c >=7.5%; age 40-79 with clinical CVD or 55-79 with subclinical CVD or >=2 risk factors; LDL-C 60-180 mg/dL; HDL-C <55 mg/dL (women, blacks) or <50 mg/dL (others); TG <750 mg/dL off lipid therapy or <400 mg/dL on lipid therapy
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Patients were specifically eligible to participate in the lipid trial if they also had the following: an LDL cholesterol level of 60 to 180 mg per deciliter (1.55 to 4.65 mmol per liter), an HDL cholesterol level below 55 mg per deciliter (1.42 mmol per liter) for women and blacks or below 50 mg per deciliter (1.29 mmol per liter) for all other groups, and a triglyceride level below 750 mg per deciliter (8.5 mmol per liter) if they were not receiving lipid therapy or below 400 mg per deciliter (4.5 mmol per liter) if they were receiving lipid therapy.
inclusion_key_criteria.note: No minimum triglyceride or maximum HDL-C beyond these broad limits: the authors say they 'used broader inclusion criteria for plasma lipid levels than might have been used if the lipid trial had been an independent study' (Discussion). Baseline median TG was only 162 mg/dL.

planned_events.note: NOT FOUND: the trial was sized by patients (5800), not by a target event count: 'The study was designed to recruit 5800 patients, with a power of 87% to detect a 20% reduction in the rate of the primary outcome ... assuming a two-sided alpha level of 0.05, a primary outcome rate of 2.4% per year in the placebo group, and an average follow-up of approximately 5.6 years' (S1, Statistical Analysis). Observed: 601 primary events.

assumed_rrr.quote: The study was designed to recruit 5800 patients, with a power of 87% to detect a 20% reduction in the rate of the primary outcome for patients in the fenofibrate group, as compared with placebo
assumed_rrr.note: Registry S3 analysis description repeats 87% power for a 20% reduction.

power.quote: with a power of 87% to detect a 20% reduction in the rate of the primary outcome

alpha.quote: assuming a two-sided alpha level of 0.05
alpha.note: O'Brien-Fleming interim monitoring; primary P value adjusted for interim analyses.

stopped_early.quote: Randomization occurred between January 11, 2001, and October 29, 2005. End-of-study visits were scheduled between March and June 2009.
stopped_early.note: Lipid trial ran to its scheduled end. (The separate ACCORD glycemia intensive arm was stopped early for mortality in 2008; registry S3.) Enrollment 5518 vs 5800 planned. The placebo event rate matched the assumption: 'the annual rate of 2.4% in the placebo group was the rate used in the power calculations' (Discussion).

baseline.note: 2.60 mmol/L. About 60% were taking a statin before enrollment; all received open-label simvastatin after randomization.
IQR 113-229 (all patients). 1.83 mmol/L. Dyslipidemic subgroup (TG >=204 and HDL-C <=34 mg/dL, 17% of patients): median TG 284 mg/dL, mean HDL-C 29.5 mg/dL (Discussion).
DERIVED, not reported: mean total cholesterol 175.2 minus mean HDL-C 38.1 = 137.1 mg/dL (3.55 mmol/L) non-HDL-C. Difference of means is valid for means, but the paper does not report non-HDL-C.
apoB baseline NOT FOUND in the main text (not reported in Table 1).

biomarker_effects.method: fasting lipid profile at the ACCORD central laboratory (LDL-C method, Friedewald vs direct, not stated in main text)
biomarker_effects.quote: By the end of the study, the mean LDL cholesterol level fell from 100.0 to 81.1 mg per deciliter (2.59 to 2.10 mmol per liter) in the fenofibrate group and from 101.1 to 80.0 mg per deciliter (2.61 to 2.07 mmol per liter) in the placebo group
biomarker_effects.note: DERIVED between-arm difference in mean change: fenofibrate -18.9 vs placebo -21.1 mg/dL = +2.2 mg/dL (+0.057 mmol/L); percent change -18.9% vs -20.9% = +2.0 points. Achieved end-of-study difference +1.1 mg/dL (81.1 vs 80.0). Not significant (Fig. 1 legend: LDL P = 0.16 at end of study). I.e. fenofibrate added no LDL-C lowering on top of simvastatin.

biomarker_effects.method: fasting lipid profile at the ACCORD central laboratory (LDL-C method, Friedewald vs direct, not stated in main text)
biomarker_effects.quote: in the fenofibrate group and from 101.1 to 80.0 mg per deciliter (2.61 to 2.07 mmol per liter) in the placebo group
biomarker_effects.note: Same derived difference in mmol/L (2.2 mg/dL / 38.67). From the paper's own mmol/L values: -0.49 vs -0.54 = +0.05 mmol/L.

biomarker_effects.method: fasting lipid profile at the ACCORD central laboratory (LDL-C method, Friedewald vs direct, not stated in main text)
biomarker_effects.quote: Mean HDL cholesterol levels increased from 38.0 to 41.2 mg per deciliter (0.98 to 1.07 mmol per liter) in the fenofibrate group and from 38.2 to 40.5 mg per deciliter (0.99 to 1.05 mmol per liter) in the placebo group.
biomarker_effects.note: DERIVED: +3.2 vs +2.3 mg/dL = +0.9 mg/dL (+0.023 mmol/L); percent +8.4% vs +6.0% (S8: 'HDL-C increased 8.4% in the fenofibrate group ... and 6.0% in the placebo group') = +2.4 points. Fig. 1 legend: HDL P = 0.01 at end of study.

biomarker_effects.method: fasting lipid profile at the ACCORD central laboratory (LDL-C method, Friedewald vs direct, not stated in main text); medians
biomarker_effects.quote: Median plasma triglyceride levels decreased from 164 to 122 mg per deciliter (1.85 to 1.38 mmol per liter) in the fenofibrate group and from 160 to 144 mg per deciliter (1.81 to 1.63 mmol per liter) in the placebo group.
biomarker_effects.note: DERIVED from medians: -42 vs -16 mg/dL = -26 mg/dL (-0.29 mmol/L); percent -25.6% vs -10.0% = -15.6 points. Difference of medians is not a median difference. Mean-based (S8 ACCORDION): -22% (187 to 145) vs -8.7% (186.2 to 170) = about -13 points. Fig. 1 legend: TG P<0.001 at 4 months and end of study.

biomarker_effects.quote: During ACCORD, triglyceride levels were reduced by 22%, from a mean of 187 mg/dL to 145 mg/dL in participants randomized to fenofibrate and declined 8.7%, from a mean of 186.2 mg/dL to 170 mg/dL in those randomized to placebo

biomarker_effects.note: NOT FOUND: placebo-adjusted non-HDL-C not reported in the NEJM main text (Fig. 1 shows total cholesterol, P=0.02 at end of study, without numbers). ACCORDION eFigure 3 and Marston 2019 (S10) Supplemental Table 2 contain it, but the supplement PDFs could not be downloaded (PMC bot check).
NOT FOUND: apoB not reported for the full ACCORD Lipid cohort in sources read.

biomarker_effects.method: median % change; combination vs simvastatin 20 mg alone
biomarker_effects.quote: From baseline to week 12, median TG levels decreased 43.0% (combination therapy) and 20.1% (simvastatin monotherapy [treatment difference -23.6%, p <0.001]).
biomarker_effects.note: Pre-readout short-term lipid RCT (n=618) of simvastatin 20 mg + fenofibrate 160 mg vs simvastatin 20 mg in combined hyperlipidemia (TG 150-500, LDL-C >130 mg/dL); used as the phase-2-equivalent lipid evidence (not a phase 2 trial of the ACCORD sponsor). Control = statin alone, as in ACCORD.

biomarker_effects.method: mean % change; combination vs simvastatin alone
biomarker_effects.quote: Mean LDL cholesterol levels decreased 31.2% and 25.8% (treatment difference -5.4%, p <0.001)
biomarker_effects.note: Baseline LDL-C >130 mg/dL, higher than ACCORD; in ACCORD the LDL-C difference was nil.

biomarker_effects.method: mean % change; combination vs simvastatin alone
biomarker_effects.quote: high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels increased 18.6% and 9.7% (treatment difference 8.8%, p <0.001)

hr.quote: The annual rate of the primary outcome was 2.2% in the fenofibrate group and 2.4% in the placebo group (hazard ratio in the fenofibrate group, 0.92; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.79 to 1.08; P = 0.32).
hr.note: Registry S3: HR 0.92 (0.79-1.08), p=0.32, Cox. No secondary outcome significant (HRs 0.82-1.17). All-cause death HR 0.91 (0.75-1.10). Prespecified subgroups: sex interaction P=0.01 (men 11.2% vs 13.3%, women 9.1% vs 6.6%); TG >=204 + HDL-C <=34 subgroup 12.4% vs 17.3% vs 10.1% vs 10.1% in others (interaction P=0.057).

p.note: Two-sided likelihood-ratio P from Cox model, adjusted for interim monitoring.

events_treatment.quote: Primary outcome (major fatal or nonfatal cardiovascular event) | 291 | 2.24 | 310 | 2.41 | 0.92 (0.79–1.08)

events_control.quote: Primary outcome (major fatal or nonfatal cardiovascular event) | 291 | 2.24 | 310 | 2.41 | 0.92 (0.79–1.08)
events_control.note: Placebo N=2753; 2.41%/yr. Registry S3: 310. Total 601 primary events.

safety_signals.value: Reversible-type serum creatinine rise with fenofibrate (0.93 to 1.10 vs 0.93 to 1.04 mg/dL); more drug discontinuation (2.4% vs 1.1%) and dose reduction (15.9% vs 7.0%) for low eGFR; no difference in ESRD/dialysis (75 vs 77)
safety_signals.quote: mean serum creatinine levels increased from 0.93 to 1.10 mg per deciliter (82 to 97 µmol per liter) in the fenofibrate group within the first year and remained relatively stable thereafter
safety_signals.note: Also: 'There was no significant between-group difference in the incidence of both hemodialysis and end-stage renal disease (75 patients in the fenofibrate group vs. 77 in the placebo group).' Less micro- and macroalbuminuria with fenofibrate.

safety_signals.value: No excess myopathy: CK >10x ULN 10 (0.4%) vs 9 (0.3%); ALT >3x ULN 52 (1.9%) vs 40 (1.5%)
safety_signals.quote: Elevations of creatine kinase of more than 10 times the upper limit of the normal range at any time during the trial occurred in 10 patients (0.4%) in the fenofibrate group and 9 (0.3%) in the placebo group
safety_signals.note: Fenofibrate, unlike gemfibrozil, does not raise statin levels (Discussion).

safety_signals.value: Possible harm in women (sex interaction P = 0.01): primary outcome 9.1% vs 6.6% in women, 11.2% vs 13.3% in men
safety_signals.quote: the primary outcome for men was 11.2% in the fenofibrate group versus 13.3% in the placebo group, whereas the rate for women was 9.1% in the fenofibrate group versus 6.6% in the placebo group (P = 0.01 for interaction)
safety_signals.note: Persisted in ACCORDION (S8: HR 1.30 women vs 0.84 men); ACCORDION authors say it 'may be a chance finding' (low placebo event rates in women).

genetics.finding: Candidate-gene study: PPARA V162 allele associated with lower and C2528 allele with higher incident nonfatal MI in 1810 type 2 diabetics (Go-DARTS)
genetics.quote: The V162 allele was associated with decreased risk of non-fatal myocardial infarction (HR = 0.31, 95%CI 0.10-0.93 p = 0.037) whereas the C2528 allele was associated with increased risk (HR = 2.77 95%CI 1.34-5.75 p = 0.006).
genetics.note: PRE-readout. Small candidate-gene study; the authors say the risk 'appears to be independent of the effect of these genotypes on lipid profiles', so it does not validate the lipid mechanism. No robust Mendelian-randomization evidence for PPARA itself found -> target genetics uncertain.

genetics.finding: Heterozygous ABCA1 loss-of-function lowers HDL-C by 17 mg/dL without raising ischemic heart disease risk
genetics.quote: Lower plasma levels of HDL cholesterol due to heterozygosity for loss-of-function mutations in ABCA1 were not associated with an increased risk of IHD.
genetics.note: PRE-readout. Europe PMC date 2008-06-01; JAMA issue 4 June 2008. Abstract read. Relevant to the HDL-raising half of the ACCORD hypothesis.

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: HDL-raising LIPG Asn396Ser and a 14-SNP HDL score not associated with MI
genetics.quote: However, a 1 SD increase in HDL cholesterol due to genetic score was not associated with risk of myocardial infarction (OR 0·93, 95% CI 0·68-1·26, p=0·63).

genetics.finding: Genetic variants affecting triglycerides (accounting for LDL-C/HDL-C) are associated with CAD in proportion to their TG effect: TG-rich lipoproteins causal
genetics.quote: These results suggest that triglyceride-rich lipoproteins causally influence risk for CAD.

genetics.finding: TG-lowering LPL variants and LDL-C-lowering LDLR variants give the same CHD protection per 10 mg/dL lower apoB; TG and LDL-C associations become null after adjusting for apoB. The authors state this explains why fibrate trials (citing ACCORD) failed: TG reductions of 20-50 mg/dL correspond to too little apoB lowering.
genetics.effect: OR 0.771 (LPL) vs 0.773 (LDLR) per 10 mg/dL lower apoB
genetics.quote: Therefore, the results of the fibrate trials appear to be explained by the modest reductions in triglyceride level and therefore the modest corresponding reductions in ApoB-containing lipoproteins observed in these studies.
genetics.note: POST-readout. Open full text (PMC6439767) read. ACCORD is reference 33 in the fibrate-trials sentence.

consensus_explanation.summary: Fenofibrate added to simvastatin did not reduce major cardiovascular events (HR 0.92, 0.79-1.08; 601 events). The between-arm lipid differences were small: LDL-C was the same in both arms (about +2 mg/dL with fenofibrate), HDL-C was only about 1 mg/dL higher, and median triglycerides were about 26 mg/dL lower on a baseline median of only 162 mg/dL. Later quantitative analyses (Ference 2019 genetics, which explicitly cite ACCORD among the fibrate trials, and the Marston 2019 trial meta-regression) concluded that fibrate benefit tracks the absolute fall in apoB/non-HDL-C, and that the modest triglyceride and apoB reductions of the fibrate trials explain their null results. So the expected effect was far below the 20% relative reduction the trial was powered for. The investigators also pointed to the broad lipid entry criteria: only the prespecified high-TG/low-HDL subgroup (17% of patients) seemed to benefit (12.4% vs 17.3%, interaction P=0.057, durable in ACCORDION, HR 0.73). That subgroup hypothesis was then weakened when PROMINENT (pemafibrate in exactly that population) showed no benefit, with apoB not lowered. The HDL-raising half of the hypothesis is not supported by genetics (ABCA1, LIPG/HDL-score Mendelian randomization). Safety was acceptable apart from a creatinine rise and an unexplained possible excess in women.

pre_readout.note: Readout = ACC presentation and NEJM online publication on 2010-03-14 (NIH press release S2). Sources with pub_date before that date counted as available.
available_before_readout: Registry record NCT00000620 with the shared primary outcome (S3, first posted 1999-10-28).
Design: 5,518-patient lipid trial, simvastatin plus fenofibrate 160 mg or placebo, LDL-C goal <100 mg/dL in both arms (S4, S5; 2007).
FIELD (fenofibrate monotherapy in 9,795 type 2 diabetics): primary coronary events HR 0.89 (0.75-1.05), with more statin drop-in on placebo (S12; 2005).
SAFARI: fenofibrate added to simvastatin 20 mg lowered TG 23.6%, LDL-C 5.4% more and raised HDL-C 8.8% more than simvastatin alone at 12 weeks (S13; 2005).
Genetics: ABCA1 loss of function lowers HDL-C without raising IHD risk (S16; 2008); small PPARA candidate-gene association with MI in diabetics (S15; 2005).
only_after_readout: Outcome HR 0.92 (0.79-1.08), events 291/310, on-treatment lipid differences, subgroups (S1; 2010-03-14 = readout day).
Investigator subgroup commentary (S7; 2011) and ACCORDION extended follow-up HR 0.93, dyslipidemic subgroup HR 0.73 (S8; 2016-12-28).
HDL Mendelian randomization (S17; 2012); TG genetics (S18; 2013); LPL vs LDLR per apoB with fibrate-trial explanation (S9; 2019).
Marston meta-regression of TG-lowering trials, RR 0.79 per 1 mmol/L non-HDL-C (S10; 2019).
PROMINENT pemafibrate null in high-TG/low-HDL type 2 diabetes (S11; 2022).

access_summary.note: Key numbers: n, follow-up, assumed RRR, power, alpha, planned events, baseline LDL-C/HDL-C/TG/apoB, LDL-C/HDL-C/TG differences, non-HDL-C and apoB differences, HR, CI low/high, p, events x2. All found numbers are in the NEJM author manuscript, which is open full text in PMC (PMC2879499, read). HR, CI, p and event counts are also in registry S3 results and the HR in press release S2. Not found: planned events (trial sized by patients), baseline apoB, placebo-adjusted non-HDL-C, placebo-adjusted apoB. Lipid differences are derived (difference of within-arm changes).

open_questions: Readout date vs press-release dateline: ACC.10 presentation and NEJM online publication were Sunday 2010-03-14, and the NIH release's text says the results appear online and are presented 'today', but the archived NIH page header says 'Monday, March 15, 2010'. readout_date and the S2 pub_date were set to 2010-03-14. If the archive builder must match the page's own dateline, use 2010-03-15 instead (one-day difference, no outcome-revealing documents in between).

Placebo-adjusted non-HDL-C and apoB for the whole cohort: NOT FOUND (NEJM Supplementary Appendix 1 Section 16, ACCORDION eFigure 3 and Marston 2019 Supplemental Table 2 were not accessible). The calculator therefore sizes the effect from LDL-C (no difference) only.

All between-arm lipid differences are derived from reported within-arm values (difference of end-of-study means or medians), not reported as differences. TG difference is from medians (-26 mg/dL, -15.6 points) in NEJM and from means (-25.8 mg/dL, -13.3 points) in ACCORDION.
LDL-C assay (Friedewald vs direct) not stated in the main text.
Planned events not reported; the trial was sized on 5800 patients, a 2.4%/yr placebo rate and 5.6 years' average follow-up (enrolled 5518; mean follow-up 4.7 y; 601 events).
Follow-up is a mean (4.7 years), median not reported.

Category choice: the investigators' contemporaneous explanation was population (broad lipid entry criteria, benefit confined to the high-TG/low-HDL subgroup). The later quantitative consensus (Ference 2019, which cites ACCORD; Marston 2019) attributes the fibrate-trial nulls to too little apoB/non-HDL-C lowering, and PROMINENT (2022) found no benefit even in the high-TG/low-HDL population. Primary set to effect_too_small, with population and biomarker_not_causal (HDL-raising rationale) as secondary.
Sex interaction (possible harm in women) remains unexplained; ACCORDION authors suggest it may be chance.
PPARA target genetics: only small candidate-gene studies found (Go-DARTS); no Mendelian randomization of PPARA itself located -> 'uncertain'.
